answer: In an agent marketplace called oasis, each identity must lock 100 copper tokens for 30 days before it can bid on jobs, and each identity may submit only one bid per auction. An attacker can forge thousands of identities, but activating 1,000 of them requires locking 100,000 tokens. The bond makes flooding auctions costly in proportion to the number of active identities, tying up capital even if no fraud is detected.
